dead_ends.tried: Using the raw <iframe src> attribute text (unresolved) as the seen-set dedup key for iframes, resolved `url` as the dedup key for <video> sources
dead_ends.why_it_failed: Inconsistent dedup key type across the two loops was a latent bug (would fail to dedupe a video file source and an iframe embed that happened to resolve to the same absolute URL, or vice versa produce false dedup misses). Fixed before committing: both loops now add the RESOLVED absolute `url` to the same `seen` Set; the YouTube/Vimeo/videoish regexes still match against the AUTHORED (unresolved) src string since query params like `?rel=0` matter less than the raw provider-URL shape, but dedup itself is resolved-URL-consistent.

dead_ends.tried: Live real-page fetch proof against several public URLs for a genuine server-rendered YouTube/Vimeo iframe
dead_ends.why_it_failed: Most candidate URLs from training-data recall 404'd (link rot). The one live 200 (w3schools html_youtube.asp) embeds the example as escaped code text, not a real tag — confirmed via direct string-context inspection, not assumed. Not a wasted attempt: it's genuine evidence the extractor behaves correctly (0 videos when none are live), but not useful as the 'found 1 real video' proof artifact, so pivoted to the brief's explicitly-sanctioned fixture-through-full-path proof instead of continuing to burn time on URL guessing.
